# Tracks

> Tracks is a free music-production studio (a DAW, digital audio workstation) that runs in a web browser at freetracks.app. There is no account, no download and no paywall. Projects, recordings and settings stay in the visitor's own browser; nothing is uploaded.

Tracks is made by JFound and is open source under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Everything runs on the Web Audio API with a custom audio engine.

What the studio does:

- Arrange: multi-track timeline, piano roll with velocity, quantize, swing, tempo map, time signatures, markers, and a session (clip-launch) view.
- Instruments: subtractive and FM synthesizer, 808 and 909 drum machines, a 16-pad sampler, and SoundFont (.sf2) playback.
- Record: microphone input or a MIDI keyboard (Web MIDI), with count-in and take comping.
- Mix: per-track parametric EQ, compressor, gate, de-esser, reverb and delay sends, group buses, sidechain ducking, and automation of any parameter.
- Vocals and audio: built-in autotune, time-stretch and repitch, and stem extraction (drums, bass, vocals, other).
- Export: WAV and MP3, per-track stems, standard MIDI file, and a self-contained .tracks.json project file.

A separate synthesizer with its own patches, effects and step sequencer runs at synth.freetracks.app.

Cost and privacy: Tracks is free to use. Google Analytics and Google AdSense load only if the visitor allows them in the site's privacy notice; music and projects are never collected either way.

## Start here

- [Tracks home](https://freetracks.app/): what Tracks is and what it can do
- [Open the studio](https://freetracks.app/studio): the music studio itself, ready in a browser tab
- [Synth](https://synth.freetracks.app/): the standalone browser synthesizer
- [Help manual](https://freetracks.app/help/): a getting-started tutorial plus every feature explained, including keyboard shortcuts
- [Privacy](https://freetracks.app/privacy): what is stored, where, and what loads only with consent

- [How to mix a track](https://freetracks.app/blog/how-to-mix-a-track-basics): EQ, compression and reverb basics
- [How to split a song into stems](https://freetracks.app/blog/split-song-into-stems): separating vocals, drums and bass
- [How to export your song to MP3 or WAV](https://freetracks.app/blog/export-song-mp3-wav): choosing a format and exporting
- [Free online music maker for students and Chromebooks](https://freetracks.app/blog/music-maker-chromebook-students): making music where software installs are blocked
- [A free GarageBand alternative](https://freetracks.app/blog/free-garageband-alternative): how Tracks compares with GarageBand
- [BandLab vs Soundtrap vs Tracks](https://freetracks.app/blog/bandlab-soundtrap-tracks-compared): three free browser studios compared
- [A free FL Studio alternative](https://freetracks.app/blog/fl-studio-alternative-browser): piano roll and pattern work in the browser
- [A free Ableton Live alternative](https://freetracks.app/blog/ableton-alternative-browser): session view and clip launching in the browser
- [Audacity vs Tracks](https://freetracks.app/blog/audacity-vs-tracks-compared): a free audio editor or a free browser DAW
